kevin_sales: Hey team — ACME's security asked for a clear ISMS scope statement and Statement of Applicability for the upcoming POC. They want to know which controls will be in-scope during the POC and what evidence we can provide.

sana_se: Got it. Quick clarifying Qs: is the POC limited to Hosted API or are they testing Private/Dedicated? That changes what evidence we can share (e.g., hosted infra vs customer-managed VPC).

acme_poc: @kevin_sales it's only Hosted API for the POC. We can use synthetic data — no PHI or PII. Main ask is: can you map Redwood's ISMS controls to our vendor risk questionnaire + provide an SoA snapshot specific to the POC scope?

maria_infosec: Thanks — hosted API + synthetic data simplifies things. We can produce: 1) A one-page ISMS scope statement that explicitly limits the POC to hosted inference endpoints and demo data; 2) A POC-specific Statement of Applicability (SoA) listing included ISO27001 controls and any exclusions with justification; 3) Evidence artifacts (policy excerpts, config screenshots, audit logs) — redacted as needed.

kevin_sales: Perfect. Customer wants the SoA and a short evidence pack within 5 business days to satisfy their InfoSec gating. Is that timeline realistic?

sana_se: 5 days should be doable if we scope the SoA to the POC only. I'll draft the SoA template and populate the following items: control mapping, responsible owners, and list of evidence we can attach. Maria — can you confirm which types of evidence are OK to share (full docs vs excerpts)?

maria_infosec: We avoid sharing full internal docs. We'll provide excerpts and signed attestations where needed. For Hosted API we can provide: network architecture diagram (public-facing), TLS cert config, data handling statement (demo-only), SoA PDF with checked controls, sample operational runbook snippets, and a redacted audit log sample. No KMS keys or sensitive logs.

acme_poc: That sounds fine. Also, they asked whether Redwood considers the POC environment within the scope of your ISO certificate or if it's explicitly excluded.

maria_infosec: Important point — the ISMS scope will state that the company ISMS covers production hosted services and related processes. For a time-limited POC using demo data we can mark the POC as 'in-scope for controls X,Y,Z' but the POC environment itself isn't a separately certified boundary. We'll include a clear applicability statement explaining that the certification applies to the production service and that evidence for the POC is provided as mapped artifacts.

kevin_sales: Action items: @sana_se draft SoA and evidence checklist (due +2 days), @maria_infosec prepare redacted artifacts and a short applicability paragraph (due +3 days). I'll send a note to ACME with the plan and timeline.

acme_poc: Thanks — we'll accept redacted evidence. Please cc our security lead when you have the SoA.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: demo tenant provisioned for acme-demo on 2026-03-25T14:00Z (info only).

sana_se: Adding: for traceability we'll include a one-page mapping table: ISO control -> Redwood control/process -> POC evidence filename. That should make vendor risk review reviewers happy.

maria_infosec: Agreed. If ACME needs a formal attestation, we can route that through legal — flag to sales if they ask for signed statements.

kevin_sales: Great — I'll loop in legal only if requested. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
